name: Biological & Geological Sciences
summary: Biological and Geological Sciences comprises flat-roofed interconnected stone laboratory wings with grouped rectangular stone-framed windows, showing three exposed rows on the bus court, five levels on the low side, rooftop stacks and exposed ducts, and one low eastern wing.

evidence.note: core-1m surface minus local ground: median 18.91 m, 90th percentile 22.26 m, maximum 28.27 m.
Western Facilities Management exterior photograph; masonry, trim and opening proportions assessed against the orthophoto.
Three tiers of pale window groups around the bus court. The return at right has deeper shade.
Sunlit stone coursing, pale multipane sash, and raised central bay with drip mould.
The service-court side exposes additional levels below the high street side; roof plant and stacks clear the parapet.
Two long north-south laboratory ranges, east green-rooflight wing and an open court. Broad ducts run along the roofs.
Mean 7 by 7 pixel PIL sample centred at normalized (0.343, 0.460) on the sunlit stone gives #ddceba.
Core terrain stands 4.2–6.4 m above the building datum along the bus court. Wall-adjacent roof samples are 17.8–18.4 m. Three upper window rows are exposed there.
Five compact core-lidar peaks align with the roof exhaust groups in the orthophoto. Their highest returns are 26.0, 28.3, 26.7, 27.6 and 27.7 metres above datum.
Two projecting stone flanks have pointed caps and frame the recessed entrance in the bus court.
At wall 6 the median surface drops from 18.4 m at the mapped wall to 6.4 m two metres outside. The low eastern lab roof also ends within two metres of mapped wall 18.
Three rows of windows face the bus court. The middle group sits in a raised bay with a single three-light window at its head and pointed stone caps on the two projecting flanks.
